nations.name: Chiricahua Apache Nation
nations.lands: Headquarters in Santa Clara, New Mexico, United States; this record describes this named community, not every Chiricahua Apache person or government

facts.text: The Chiricahua Apache Nation describes its governance through an Executive Council and National Council made up of citizen-descendants.
facts.evidence: Executive Council and National Council are comprised of citizen-descendants

facts.text: The Chiricahua Apache Nation lists its tribal headquarters in Santa Clara, New Mexico.
facts.evidence: Santa Clara, NM USA 88022

facts.text: Its foundation's stated work includes education, social welfare and defending Chiricahua Apache self-determination.
facts.evidence: Promote unity, solidarity, and social welfare

nations.name: Lipan Apache Tribe
nations.lands: Texas, United States, with tribal administration in McAllen and historical homelands spanning Texas and northern Mexico

facts.text: The Lipan Apache Tribe in Texas maintains a Tribal Council responsible for community welfare and protection of its heritage.
facts.evidence: a governing body, the Tribal Council

facts.text: The Tribe recounts that by 1880, Lipan communities lived along the Rio Grande on both sides of the United States-Mexico border.
facts.evidence: both sides of the border

facts.text: In 2021, the City and County of Presidio donated a Lipan cemetery parcel to the Lipan Apache Tribe.

source.title: El Cementerio de los Lipanes Transferred to Tribe

facts.evidence: donated by the City of Presidio and the County

nations.name: Mescalero Apache
nations.lands: South-central New Mexico, US (Mescalero Apache Reservation)

facts.text: Chiricahua Apache families arrived at the Mescalero reservation in 1913 after imprisonment at Fort Sill, Oklahoma.
facts.evidence: In 1913, approximately 200 members of the Chiricahua band

nations.name: Southern Ute Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Southern Ute Reservation around Ignacio, southwestern Colorado, United States

facts.text: The Southern Ute Indian Tribe is made up of the Mouache and Caputa bands and is headquartered in Ignacio, Colorado.
facts.evidence: Mouache and Caputa bands comprise the Southern Ute Tribe

facts.text: Southern Ute government is based on a constitution adopted in 1936 and revised in 1975.
facts.evidence: Tribal Constitution adopted November 4, 1936

facts.text: An elected Tribal Council governs the Southern Ute Indian Tribe, which maintains its own constitution, laws and tribal courts.
facts.evidence: constitution, code of laws, and a tribal court system

facts.text: The Tribe's Brunot Area guide explains the hunting right reserved in the 1873 agreement, despite the loss of reservation lands.
facts.evidence: an important provision reserving for the Utes the right

nations.name: Tonto Apache Tribe
nations.lands: Payson, Gila County, Arizona, United States

facts.text: The Tonto Apache Tribe is based beside Payson in northwestern Gila County, Arizona.
facts.evidence: located adjacent to the town of Payson

facts.text: In 1875, Tonto and Yavapai people were forcibly moved from the Rio Verde Reserve to San Carlos. Some Tonto families later returned to Payson.
facts.evidence: forcibly moved to the San Carlos Apache Reservation

facts.text: In 2010, land for the Tonto Apache Tribe was acquired in trust following a land exchange with the U.S. Forest Service.

source.title: Reservation proclamation for trust land belonging to the Tonto Apache Tribe of Arizona

facts.evidence: parcel was acquired in trust in 2010

nations.name: Ute Indian Tribe
also: Ute Indian Tribe of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation
nations.lands: Uintah and Ouray Reservation, northeastern Utah, with tribal government at Fort Duchesne, United States

facts.text: The Ute Indian Tribe elects Business Committee representatives from the Uintah, Uncompahgre and Whiteriver bands.
facts.evidence: The Uintah, Uncompahgre and Whiteriver bands

facts.text: The Tribe delegates protection, restoration and management of Uintah and Ouray Reservation water resources to its Water Resources Department and Commission.
facts.evidence: protect, restore, develop, manage, and maintain the water resources

facts.text: In 1881, the United States forcibly removed White River Utes from Colorado to the Uintah Reservation.

source.title: Ute Indians
source.publisher: Utah Division of State History, History to Go

facts.evidence: from Colorado to the Uintah Reservation

facts.text: In an April 2026 statement, the Ute Indian Tribe announced it would appeal a federal district court decision concerning split-estate reservation lands.

source.title: Tribe will appeal Utah Federal District Court decision on split estate lands

facts.evidence: Tribe will appeal Utah Federal District Court

nations.name: Ute Mountain Ute Tribe
nations.lands: Towaoc and reservation lands in southwestern Colorado and northwestern New Mexico; White Mesa, Utah, United States

facts.text: The Ute Mountain Ute Tribe identifies itself as the Weenuche band of the Ute Nation, with its tribal offices in Towaoc, Colorado.
facts.evidence: are the Weenuche band of the Ute Nation

facts.text: The Weenuche Band organized a tribal government and adopted a constitution six years after the Indian Reorganization Act of 1934.
facts.evidence: organized a tribal government and enacted a tribal constitution

facts.text: The Ute Mountain Ute Tribal Council is elected by the tribal membership and governs the reservation.
facts.evidence: elected by popular vote of Tribal membership

facts.text: White Mesa Administration supports community members with employment, education and access to basic services in White Mesa, Utah.
facts.evidence: support to all White Mesa community members
